label.en: Lang of the Ministry of Personnel

units.zh: 邢卲，字子才，河間鄚人，魏太常貞之後。
units.en: Biography of Xing Shao. Xing Shao, styled Zicai, was from Mo in Hejian commandery; he descended from Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhen of Wei.
units.literal: Xing Shao, styled Zicai, a man of Mo in Hejian, descendant of Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhen.

units.zh: 父虬，魏光祿卿。
units.en: His father Xing Qiu had served Wei as director of the imperial household.
units.literal: His father Qiu was Wei Director of the Imperial Household.

units.zh: 卲小字吉，少時有避，遂不行名。
units.en: Shao's childhood name was Ji; while young he observed a naming taboo and did not use his formal name.
units.literal: Shao's childhood name was Ji; in youth there was a taboo, and so he did not use his formal name.

units.zh: 年五歲，魏吏部郎清河崔亮見而奇之，曰：「此子後當大成，位望通顯。」
units.en: At five, Cui Liang of Qinghe, a lang in the Wei ministry of personnel, saw him and marveled, saying, "This child will one day achieve great things; office and fame will spread far and wide."
units.literal: At age five, Cui Liang of Qinghe, Lang of the Ministry of Personnel in Wei, saw him and was struck, saying: "This boy will in time achieve great things; rank and repute will be universally manifest."

units.zh: 十歲便能屬文，雅有才思，聰明強記，日誦萬餘言。
units.en: By ten he could write compositions; gifted and inventive, sharp-witted and retentive, he recited more than ten thousand words each day.
units.literal: At ten he could compose in writing; elegant in talent and thought, clever and with a strong memory, he recited more than ten thousand words a day.

units.zh: 族兄巒，有人倫鑒，謂子弟曰：「宗室中有此兒，非常人也。」
units.en: His kinsman Luan, skilled at judging men, told the younger generation, "Our house has produced this boy—he is no ordinary person."
units.literal: His clansman Luan, who had judgment of human character, told the younger kin: "In our lineage there is this boy—a man not of the common sort."

units.zh: 少在洛陽，會天下無事，與時名勝專以山水遊宴為娛，不暇勤業。
units.en: While young in Luoyang, the empire was quiet; with celebrated contemporaries he gave himself only to landscape outings and banquets, leaving no time for steady application.
units.literal: In youth he was in Luoyang; the realm was at peace, and with the day's eminent men he devoted himself solely to touring mountains and waters and feasting for pleasure, with no leisure for diligent study.

units.zh: 嘗因霖雨，乃讀《漢書》，五日，略能遍記之。
units.en: Once, during long rains, he took up the History of Han and within five days could recall most of it.
units.literal: Once during prolonged rain he read the History of Han; in five days he could largely remember it through.

units.zh: 後因飲謔倦，方廣尋經史，五行俱下，一覽便記，無所遺忘。
units.en: Later, tired of drink and banter, he turned widely to the classics and histories; reading five lines at a glance, he retained each passage at once.
units.literal: Later, wearied of drinking and jesting, he broadly sought out the classics and histories; with five lines at once under his eye, one reading and he remembered—nothing was lost.

units.zh: 文章典麗，既贍且速。
units.en: His writing was elegant and polished, copious yet quick.
units.literal: His compositions were classical and beautiful, ample yet swift.

units.zh: 年未二十，名動衣冠。
units.en: Before twenty his reputation had shaken the official class.
units.literal: Before he was twenty his name stirred the gentry.

units.zh: 嘗與右北平陽固、河東裴伯茂、從兄罘、河南陸道暉等至北海王昕舍宿飲，相與賦詩，凡數十首，皆在主人奴處。
units.en: Once he stayed overnight drinking at Prince Xin of Beihai's residence with Yang Gu of Youbeiping, Pei Bomo of Hedong, his paternal cousin Fei, and Lu Daohui of Henan; they composed several dozen poems together, all left with the host's servant.
units.literal: He once lodged and drank overnight at the house of the Prince of Beihai, Xin, with Youbeiping Yang Gu, Hedong Pei Bomo, his cousin from the father's line Fei, and Henan Lu Daohui; together they composed poems, several dozen in all, and all were left with the host's servant.

units.zh: 旦日奴行，諸人求詩不得，卲皆為誦之。
units.en: At dawn the servant went abroad; the others could not find their poems, but Shao recited them all.
units.literal: Next morning the servant went out; the others could not recover their poems, but Shao recited every one from memory.

units.zh: 諸人有不認詩者，奴還得本，不誤一字。
units.en: Some did not recognize their own work; when the servant brought back the originals, not one character differed.
units.literal: Some among them did not recognize their own poems; when the servant returned with the originals, not a single character was wrong.

units.zh: 諸人方之王粲。
units.en: The company then compared him to Wang Can.
units.literal: The company thereupon ranked him with Wang Can.

units.zh: 吏部尚書隴西李神儁大相欽重，引為忘年之交。
units.en: Li Shenjun of Longxi, minister of personnel, held him in high regard and took him as a friend despite the age gap.
units.literal: Li Shenjun of Longxi, Minister of Personnel, greatly esteemed him and made him a friend across the years.

units.zh: 釋巾為魏宣武挽郎，除奉朝請，遷著作佐郎。
units.en: Leaving mourning, he served as a Wei mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu, was made gentleman attendant at court, and rose to assistant editorial director.
units.literal: He doffed mourning and became a Wei mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu, was appointed gentleman attendant at court, and was promoted Assistant Editorial Director.

units.zh: 深為領軍元叉所禮，叉新除尚書令，神儁與陳郡袁翻在席，叉令卲作謝表，須臾便成，以示諸賓。
units.en: The commander of the guards Yuan Cha treated him with great respect; when Cha had just become director of the masters of writing, Shenjun and Yuan Fan of Chen were present, and Cha had Shao write a letter of thanks—it was finished at once and shown round.
units.literal: He was deeply honored by the commander of the guards Yuan Cha; when Cha had just been appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, Shenjun and Yuan Fan of Chen commandery were at the feast, and Cha had Shao draft a letter of thanks—in a moment it was done, and shown to the guests.

units.zh: 神儁曰：「邢卲此表，足使袁公變色。」
units.en: Shenjun said, "This table from Xing Shao alone would make Master Yuan flush."
units.literal: Shenjun said: "This memorial of Xing Shao's is enough to make Master Yuan change color."

units.zh: 孝昌初，與黃門侍郎李琰之對典朝儀。
units.en: At the opening of Xiaochang he and yellow gate attendant Li Yanzhi jointly directed court ceremonial.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he and Yellow Gate Attendant Li Yanzhi jointly oversaw court ritual.

units.zh: 自孝明之後，文雅大盛，卲雕蟲之美，獨步當時，每一文初出，京師為之紙貴，讀誦俄遍遠近。
units.en: After Emperor Xiaoming of Wei, literary culture flourished; Shao's ornamental prose stood alone—each new piece made paper dear in the capital, and within moments it was read and recited across the realm.
units.literal: After Emperor Xiaoming, letters flourished greatly; Shao's ornamental beauty in writing stood alone in his age—whenever a piece first appeared, the capital ran short of paper for it, and within moments it was read and chanted near and far.

units.zh: 于時袁翻與范陽祖瑩位望通顯，文筆之美，見稱先達，以卲藻思華贍，深共嫉之。
units.en: Yuan Fan and Zu Ying of Fanyang were then eminent in office and fame, their writing praised by seniors; Shao's lush brilliance they jointly resented.
units.literal: At the time Yuan Fan and Zu Ying of Fanyang, lofty in rank and repute, were praised by elders for the beauty of their brush; seeing Shao's florid, brilliant thought, they deeply envied him together.

units.zh: 每洛中貴人拜職，多憑卲為謝表。
units.en: Whenever a Luoyang grandee assumed a new post, he usually had Shao draft the letter of thanks.
units.literal: Whenever a noble in Luoyang took a new post, he mostly relied on Shao for the letter of thanks.

units.zh: 嘗有一貴勝初受官，大集賓食，翻與卲俱在坐。
units.en: Once a powerful man had just received appointment and held a great banquet; Fan and Shao were both present.
units.literal: Once a powerful man had just received office and gave a great feast for guests; Fan and Shao were both seated.

units.zh: 翻意主人托其為讓表，遂命卲作之。
units.en: Fan assumed the host meant him to write the declination and ordered Shao to do it instead.
units.literal: Fan supposed the host had entrusted him with the declination memorial and thereupon ordered Shao to write it.

units.zh: 翻甚不悅，每告人云：「邢家小兒當客作章表，自買黃紙，寫而送之。」
units.en: Fan was deeply displeased and often said, "That Xing boy ought to write his own memorials as a guest—buy his own yellow paper, draft it, and submit it himself."
units.literal: Fan was very displeased and often told others: "The Xing boy should, when a guest, compose his own memorials—buy his own yellow paper, write it, and send it in."

units.zh: 卲恐為翻所害，乃辭以疾。
units.en: Shao feared Fan would injure him and pleaded illness.
units.literal: Shao feared harm from Fan and pleaded illness.

units.zh: 屬尚書令元羅出鎮青州，啟為府司馬。
units.en: When director of the masters of writing Yuan Luo took command of Qing province, he had Shao appointed headquarters staff secretary.
units.literal: When Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo went out to command Qing province, he recommended Shao as staff secretary of the headquarters.

units.zh: 遂在青土，終日酣賞，盡山泉之致。
units.en: He stayed in the east, feasting and savoring all day, draining every delight of hill and stream.
units.literal: He remained in the eastern lands, drinking and enjoying himself all day, exhausting the charm of mountains and springs.

units.zh: 永安初，累遷中書侍郎，所作詔誥，文體宏麗。
units.en: At the beginning of Yong'an he rose repeatedly to secretariat attendant; his edicts and pronouncements were magnificent in diction.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was promoted repeatedly to Secretariat Attendant; the edicts and pronouncements he drafted were grand and beautiful in style.

units.zh: 及尒朱榮入洛，京師擾亂，卲與弘農楊愔避地嵩高山。
units.en: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the capital fell into chaos, Shao and Yang Yin of Hongnong fled to Mount Song.
units.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang the capital was in turmoil; Shao and Yang Yin of Hongnong took refuge on Mount Song.

units.zh: 普泰中，兼給事黃門侍郎，尋為散騎常侍。
units.en: In Putai he was made concurrent attendant of the yellow gate in the secretariat, then regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
units.literal: In Putai he was concurrently Attendant of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat; soon after he became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

units.zh: 太昌初，勑令恒直內省，給御食，令覆按尚書門下事，凡除大官，先問其可否，然後施行。
units.en: At the beginning of Taichang he was ordered to keep constant watch in the inner court, supplied with imperial food, and told to review business of the masters of writing and secretariat; major appointments were first referred to him for approval.
units.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was ordered to remain constantly on duty in the inner court, given imperial meals, and charged to review affairs of the Masters of Writing and the Secretariat; for every great appointment he was first asked whether it was permissible, and only then was it carried out.

units.zh: 除衛將軍、國子祭酒。
units.en: He was made general of the guards and grand master of the imperial academy.
units.literal: He was appointed General of the Guards and Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 以親老還鄉，詔所在特給兵力五人，並令歲一入朝，以備顧問。
units.en: When his parents grew old he went home; the throne ordered his district to assign him five guards and to let him attend court once a year for consultation.
units.literal: Because his parents were aged he returned home; an edict ordered the locality to grant him especially five soldiers of force, and also to enter court once a year as adviser.

units.zh: 丁母憂，哀毀過禮。
units.en: Mourning his mother, he grieved beyond what the rites prescribed.
units.literal: On observing mourning for his mother his grief exceeded the rites.

units.zh: 後楊愔與魏收及卲請置學及修立明堂，奏曰：
units.en: Later Yang Yin, Wei Shou, and Shao petitioned to establish schools and rebuild the Bright Hall, writing:
units.literal: Later Yang Yin with Wei Shou and Shao requested the establishment of schools and the repair and erection of the Bright Hall, memorializing:

units.zh: 世室明堂，顯於周、夏；
units.en: The Ancestral Chamber and Bright Hall shone forth under Zhou and Xia;
units.literal: The Ancestral Chamber and Bright Hall were illustrious in Zhou and Xia;

units.zh: 一黌兩學，盛自虞、殷。
units.en: a single academy and paired schools flourished from Yu and Yin.
units.literal: one academy and two schools flourished from the time of Yu and Yin.

units.zh: 所以宗配上帝，以著莫大之嚴；
units.en: By them the realm sacrificed to the Lord on High and showed the greatest solemnity;
units.literal: Thereby to sacrifice to the Lord on High and display the utmost majesty;

units.zh: 宣布下土，以彰則天之軌。
units.en: they proclaimed to the four quarters and embodied Heaven's model of rule.
units.literal: to proclaim across the lower realm and manifest the pattern of matching Heaven.

units.zh: 養黃發以詢哲言，育青衿而敷教典，用能享國長久，風徽萬祀者也。
units.en: They nourished gray hair to seek wisdom and reared blue collars to spread the teaching canon—thus realms endured and their fame lasted ten thousand generations.
units.literal: To nourish white-haired elders in seeking wise words, to rear blue-collared youths in spreading the teaching canon—thereby states enjoyed long endurance and their emblems through ten thousand sacrifices.

units.zh: 爰暨亡秦，改革其道，坑儒滅學，以蔽黔黎。
units.en: Then Qin fell, altered the Way, buried scholars and ended learning, and darkened the common folk.
units.literal: When it reached the fallen Qin, it reformed their Way, buried the ru and extinguished learning, to blind the black-haired people.

units.zh: 故九服分崩，祚終二代。
units.en: The nine domains shattered and the throne passed after only two generations.
units.literal: Hence the nine domains split apart and the mandate ended after two generations.

units.zh: 炎漢勃興，更修儒術。
units.en: Han rose in flame and again restored Confucian learning.
units.literal: The blazing Han rose vigorously and again repaired ru learning.

units.zh: 故西京有六學之義，東都有三本之盛。
units.en: In the western capital stood the six schools; in the eastern capital the glory of three academies.
units.literal: Hence in the Western Capital were the meaning of six schools; in the Eastern Capital the splendor of three academies.

units.zh: 逮自魏、晉，撥亂相因，兵革之中，學校不絕。
units.en: From Wei and Jin onward, rebellion followed rebellion, yet amid war the schools never ceased.
units.literal: Down through Wei and Jin, in turmoil one after another, amid arms and armor the schools did not perish.

units.zh: 仰惟高祖孝文皇帝稟聖自天，道鏡今古，列校序於鄉黨，敦詩書於郡國。
units.en: We look up to Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, the High Ancestor, who received the sage from Heaven and whose Way reflects all ages—he ordered schools in the hamlets and spread the Odes and Documents through every commandery.
units.literal: Looking up, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, the High Ancestor, received the sage from Heaven; his Way mirrors present and past; he arrayed schools in the districts and thickly spread the Odes and Documents through the commanderies.

units.zh: 但經始事殷，戎軒屢駕，未遑多就，弓劍弗追。
units.en: Yet the founding work pressed hard and the war chariot rode out again and again; he had no leisure to finish—bow and sword were left behind.
units.literal: But the founding enterprise was pressing, the martial chariot was repeatedly driven forth; there was no leisure to accomplish much—the bow and sword could not be followed up.

units.zh: 世宗統歷，聿遵先緒，永平之中，大興板築。
units.en: Emperor Shizong of Wei took up the former thread; in Yongping he launched great construction.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong of Wei continued the former thread; in Yongping he greatly raised timber and earthworks.

units.zh: 續以水旱，戎馬生郊，雖逮為山，還停一簣。
units.en: Then flood and drought came, war-horses at the suburbs; though the mound was nearly made, one basket of earth remained undone.
units.literal: Then came flood and drought, war-horses at the suburbs; though the mountain was nearly heaped, one basket of earth still halted.

units.zh: 而明堂禮樂之本，乃鬱荊棘之林；
units.en: The root of rites and music, the Bright Hall, became a tangle of thorns;
units.literal: Yet the root of Bright Hall, rites and music, became a thicket of brambles and thorns;

units.zh: 膠序德義之基，空盈牧豎之跡；
units.en: the school halls, foundation of virtue and duty, stood empty but for herd-boys' footprints;
units.literal: the foundation of virtue and righteousness in the school halls stood empty, filled only with the tracks of herd-boys;

units.zh: 城隍嚴固之重，闕磚石之功；
units.en: the ramparts, weight of defense, lacked brick and stone;
units.literal: the weight of stern ramparts and walls lacked the work of brick and stone;

units.zh: 墉構顯望之要，少樓榭之飾。
units.en: the lofty terraces that display imperial majesty had scarcely tower or pavilion.
units.literal: the essentials of lofty terraces and structures had little adornment of towers and pavilions.

units.zh: 加以風雨稍侵，漸致虧墜。
units.en: Wind and rain wore at them until they crumbled.
units.literal: Added to this, wind and rain gradually encroached, and bit by bit they fell into ruin.

units.zh: 非所謂追隆堂構，儀刑萬國者也。
units.en: This is not to pursue a lofty hall nor to make ritual the model for ten thousand states.
units.literal: This is not what is called pursuing the loftiness of the hall's frame and taking the rites as model for ten thousand states.

units.zh: 伏聞朝議以高祖大造區夏，道侔姬文，提記明堂，式配上帝。
units.en: We hear the court argues that because the High Ancestor shaped the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, he raised the Bright Hall to sacrifice to the Lord on High.
units.literal: We have heard that court discussion, because the High Ancestor greatly fashioned the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, raised the record of the Bright Hall to match the Lord on High.

units.zh: 今若基址不修，乃同丘畎，即使高皇神享，闕於國陽，宗事之典，有聲無實。
units.en: If the foundations are not restored, it is but a mound in a field—even the High Emperor's spirit lacks its seat in the national altar; ancestral rite has sound without substance.
units.literal: If now the foundation is not repaired, it is the same as a hillock in a field; even if the High Emperor's spirit is offered to, it is lacking at the national yang; the canon of ancestral service has sound without substance.

units.zh: 此臣子所以匪寧，億兆所以佇望也。
units.en: Hence ministers cannot rest and the people wait in hope.
units.literal: This is why ministers and sons are uneasy and the hundred millions stand waiting.

units.zh: 臣又聞官方授能，所以任事，事既任矣，酬之以祿。
units.en: We also hear that office grants ability to bear tasks, and tasks once borne are repaid with salary.
units.literal: Your subject has also heard that the official realm grants ability so as to charge with affairs; once charged, salary rewards the service.

units.zh: 如此則上無曠官之譏，下絕尸素之謗。
units.en: Then above none blame vacant posts; below none mock salary without work.
units.literal: Thus above there is no censure of vacant posts; below there is no slander of those who eat salary and do nothing.

units.zh: 今國子雖有學官之名，無教授之實，何異兔絲燕麥，南箕北斗哉？
units.en: Today the imperial academy bears the name of a teaching office yet has no teaching—no different from dodder on wheat, or the Winnow Basket and Northern Dipper stars.
units.literal: Now the Imperial Academy, though it has the name of a school office, has no reality of instruction—how is it different from dodder on wheat, or the Winnow Basket and Northern Dipper?

units.zh: 昔劉向有言，王者宜興辟雍、陳禮樂以風天下。
units.en: Liu Xiang once said a king should raise the Bright Academy and display rites and music to sway the realm.
units.literal: Formerly Liu Xiang said that a king should raise the Bright Academy and display rites and music to transform the realm.

units.zh: 夫禮樂所以養人，刑法所以殺人，而有司勤勤，請定刑法，至於禮樂，則曰未敢。
units.en: Rites and music nourish men; penal law kills them—yet officials press eagerly to fix penal law, while of rites and music they say they dare not.
units.literal: Rites and music are for nourishing men; penal law is for killing men—yet the offices are diligent in requesting the fixing of penal law, while of rites and music they say they dare not yet.

units.zh: 是敢於殺人，不敢於養人也。
units.en: They dare kill but dare not nourish.
units.literal: This is daring to kill men and not daring to nourish men.

units.zh: 臣以為當今四海清平，九服寧宴，經國要重，理應先榮，脫復稽延，則劉向之言徵矣。
units.en: We hold that with the four seas calm and the nine domains at peace, the state's first duty should be honored—delay again, and Liu Xiang's warning will come true.
units.literal: Your subject considers that now within the four seas all is clear and level, the nine domains tranquil and feasting; the essentials of governing the state ought first to be honored—if again delayed, Liu Xiang's words will prove true.

units.zh: 但事不兩興，須有進退。
units.en: Yet two great works cannot rise together; there must be choice between advance and retreat.
units.literal: But two things cannot be raised at once; advance and retreat must be chosen.

units.zh: 以臣愚量，宜罷尚方雕靡之作，頗省永寧土木之功，並減瑤光材瓦之力，兼分石窟鐫琢之勞，及諸事役非世急者，三時農隙，修此數條。
units.en: In our humble judgment, stop the directorate's ornamental works, cut Yongning's timber and earth, reduce Yaoguang's tile and timber, divide the labor of the stone grottoes, and every task not urgent to the age; in the three seasons' farming gaps, repair these several works.
units.literal: By your subject's dull reckoning, one should stop the ornate works of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories, considerably reduce the timber-and-earth projects of Yongning, likewise cut the tile-and-timber of Yaoguang, share out the labor of carving the stone grottoes, and all other tasks not urgent to the age; in the three seasons' gaps in farming, repair these several items.

units.zh: 使辟雍之禮，蔚爾而復興；
units.en: Then Bright Hall ritual will flourish again;
units.literal: Then the rites of the Bright Academy will luxuriantly revive;

units.zh: 諷誦之音，煥然而更作，美榭高墉嚴壯於外，槐宮棘寺顯麗於中。
units.en: chanting and recitation will blaze anew; fine towers and high walls will stand stern without, the academy and law courts bright within.
units.literal: the sound of chanting and recitation will blaze forth anew; fine terraces and high walls will be stern and strong without, the locust palace and thorn offices bright and splendid within.

units.zh: 更明古今，重遵鄉飲，敦進郡學，精課經業，如此則元、凱可得之於上序，遊、夏可致之於下國，豈不休歟！
units.en: Clarify past and present, restore district drinking, advance commandery schools, test classic learning—then Yuan and Kai may appear in the capital schools, You and Xia in the provinces; would that not be glorious!
units.literal: Further clarify past and present, again honor district drinking, urge forward commandery schools, examine closely classic studies—thus Yuan and Kai may be obtained in the upper sequence, You and Xia brought forth in the lower states; would it not be glorious!

units.zh: 靈太後令曰：「配饗大禮，為國之本，此以戎馬在郊，未遑修繕。
units.en: Empress Dowager Ling ordered, "The great rite of matching sacrifice is the root of the state; war-horses at the suburbs left no leisure for repair.
units.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "The great rite of matching sacrifice is the root of the state; because war-horses were at the suburbs, repair could not be hurried.

units.zh: 今四表晏寧，當勅有司，別議經始。」
units.en: Now the four quarters are calm; let the proper offices separately plan the founding work."
units.literal: Now the four quarters are tranquil and secure; the relevant offices should be ordered separately to deliberate on the founding enterprise."

units.zh: 累遷太常卿、中書監，攝國子祭酒。
units.en: He rose repeatedly to grand master of ceremonies and secretariat supervisor, acting grand master of the imperial academy.
units.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand Master of Ceremonies and Secretariat Supervisor, acting Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 是時朝臣多守一職，帶領二官甚少，卲頓居三職，並是文學之首，當世榮之。
units.en: Most ministers then held one post; few bore two—Shao at once held three, each at the summit of literary office, and his contemporaries envied him.
units.literal: At the time many court ministers held a single office; few concurrently led two posts—Shao suddenly held three, all at the head of letters, and the age honored him.

units.zh: 文宣幸晉陽，路中頻有甘露之瑞，朝臣皆作《甘露頌》，尚書符令卲為之序。
units.en: Gao Yang visited Jinyang; along the way sweet dew appeared again and again; court ministers all wrote Sweet Dew Eulogies, and the masters of writing had Shao compose the preface.
units.literal: Gao Yang visited Jinyang; on the road sweet dew repeatedly appeared as an omen; the court ministers all composed "Sweet Dew Eulogies," and the Masters of Writing ordered Shao to write the preface.

units.zh: 及文宣皇帝崩，凶禮多見訊訪，勑撰哀策。
units.en: When Emperor Wenxuan died, he was much consulted on funeral rites and ordered to draft the lamentation.
units.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan died, in the dire rites he was much consulted; he was ordered to draft the lamentation.

units.zh: 後授特進，卒。
units.en: Later he was granted special advance and died.
units.literal: Later he was given Special Advance and died.

units.zh: 卲率情簡素，內行修謹，兄弟親姻之間，稱為雍睦。
units.en: Shao was plain by nature, careful in private conduct, and among brothers and in-laws was praised for harmony.
units.literal: Shao followed his nature in plain simplicity; inward conduct was careful and reverent; among brothers and affinal kin he was called harmonious.

units.zh: 博覽墳籍，無不通曉，晚年尤以《五經》章句為意，窮其指要。
units.en: He read widely in the classics and histories without exception; in later years he especially pursued the Five Classics in chapter and comment, plumbing their core.
units.literal: He broadly read the classics and histories and was versed in all; in later years he especially took to the chapter-and-sentence meaning of the Five Classics and exhausted their essentials.

units.zh: 吉兇禮儀，公私諮稟，質疑去惑，為世指南。
units.en: On ritual, public or private, he was consulted; he cleared doubt and served as the age's guide.
units.literal: For auspicious and inauspicious ritual, public and private, he was consulted; doubts were resolved and confusion removed—he was the age's compass.

units.zh: 每公卿會議，事關典故，卲援筆立成，證引該洽。
units.en: Whenever ministers debated precedent, Shao wrote at once, citations full and apt.
units.literal: Whenever the high ministers met in council on matters touching precedent, Shao took brush and finished at once, citations ample and fitting.

units.zh: 帝命朝章，敢定俄頃。
units.en: Imperial edicts and court regulations he could settle in moments.
units.literal: Edicts and court regulations from the emperor he dared fix in a moment.

units.zh: 詞致宏遠，獨步當時。
units.en: His diction was vast and far-reaching, unmatched in his day.
units.literal: His phrasing was grand and far-reaching, standing alone in his time.

units.zh: 與濟陰溫子升為文士之冠，世論謂之溫、邢。
units.en: With Wen Zisheng of Jiyin he stood at the head of men of letters; contemporaries called them Wen and Xing.
units.literal: With Wen Zisheng of Jiyin he was crown of literary men; the age called them Wen and Xing.

units.zh: 鉅鹿魏收，雖天才艷發，而年事在二人之後，故子升死後，方稱邢、魏焉。
units.en: Wei Shou of Julu, though brilliant by nature, was junior to both; only after Zisheng died were Xing and Wei named together.
units.literal: Wei Shou of Julu, though his heaven-given talent blazed forth, was younger in years than the two; only after Zisheng's death was Xing and Wei spoken of.

units.zh: 雖望實兼重，不以才位傲物。
units.en: Though heavy in repute and office, he did not condescend with talent or rank.
units.literal: Though rank and substance were both weighty, he did not use talent and office to look down on others.

units.zh: 脫略簡易，不修威儀，車服器用，充事而已。
units.en: He was informal and easy, cared nothing for pomp; carriage, dress, and gear sufficed and no more.
units.literal: Careless and easy, he did not cultivate imposing manner; carriage, dress, and implements were only enough to serve.

units.zh: 有齋不居，坐臥恒在一小屋。
units.en: While fasting he avoided the main rooms; sitting or lying, he kept to one small chamber.
units.literal: When fasting he did not occupy the main rooms; sitting or lying he was always in one small chamber.

units.zh: 果餌之屬，或置之梁上，賓至，下而共噉。
units.en: Fruit he sometimes stored on the rafters; when guests arrived he lowered it and shared it.
units.literal: Fruit and the like he sometimes set on the rafters; when guests came he lowered them and they ate together.

units.zh: 天姿質素，特安異同，士無賢愚，皆能顧接，對客或解衣覓蝨，且與劇談。
units.en: His nature was plain; he was at ease with all sorts; worthy or dull, every gentleman met his courtesy; with guests he might open his robe to pick lice and still talk fiercely.
units.literal: Heaven's gift was plain substance; he was especially at ease with difference and sameness; gentlemen whether worthy or foolish he could all receive; facing guests he sometimes undid his robe to hunt lice, yet still held fierce talk.

units.zh: 有書甚多，而不甚讐校。
units.en: He owned many books but seldom collated them.
units.literal: He had very many books but did not much collate them.

units.zh: 見人校書，常笑曰：「何愚之甚，天下書至死讀不可遍，焉能復校此。
units.en: Seeing others collate books, he would laugh and say, "How foolish—no one can read every book under Heaven to the end; why collate these again?
units.literal: Seeing others collate books, he often laughed and said: "How very foolish—books under Heaven cannot all be read to the end; how could one again collate these?

units.zh: 且誤書思之，更是一適。」
units.en: Besides, to ponder a mistaken book is its own pleasure."
units.literal: Moreover, to think on a mistaken book is again a kind of pleasure."

units.zh: 妻弟李季節，才學之士，謂子才曰：「世間人多不聰明，思誤書何由能得。」
units.en: His wife's brother Li Jijie, a scholar, said to Zicai, "Most people are not clever—how can pondering mistaken books gain anything?"
units.literal: His wife's younger brother Li Jijie, a man of talent and learning, said to Zicai: "Most men in the world are not clever—how could thinking on mistaken books obtain anything?"

units.zh: 子才曰：「若思不能得，便不勞讀書。」
units.en: Zicai said, "If thought cannot obtain it, then there is no need to trouble over books at all."
units.literal: Zicai said: "If by thinking one cannot obtain it, then there is no need to labor at reading books."

units.zh: 與婦甚疏，未嘗內宿。
units.en: He was distant from his wife and never slept inside with her.
units.literal: With his wife he was very distant and never spent a night within.

units.zh: 自云嘗晝入內閤，為狗所吠，言畢便撫掌大笑。
units.en: He said he once entered the inner quarters by day and was barked at by a dog; saying this, he clapped his hands and laughed.
units.literal: He himself said he once entered the inner apartments by day and was barked at by a dog; having spoken he at once clapped his hands and laughed greatly.

units.zh: 性好談賞，不能閑獨，公事歸休，恒須賓客自伴。
units.en: He loved conversation and could not sit alone; when office ended and he was at leisure, he always wanted guests beside him.
units.literal: His nature loved talk and appreciation and could not be idle alone; when public business ended and he rested, he always needed guests for company.

units.zh: 事寡嫂甚謹，養孤子恕，慈受特深。
units.en: He cared for his widowed sister-in-law with scrupulous devotion and raised the orphan Shu with an affection that ran unusually deep.
units.literal: In serving his widowed sister-in-law he was most careful; in raising the orphan son Shu, his kindness and acceptance ran especially deep.

units.zh: 在兗州，有都信云恕疾，便憂之，廢寢食，顏色貶損。
units.en: While stationed in Yan province, he heard from a capital courier that Shu had fallen ill and was seized with worry at once—he stopped eating and sleeping, and his face grew haggard.
units.literal: While in Yan province, when a capital messenger reported that Shu was ill, he at once grew anxious, abandoned sleep and food, and his complexion faded.

units.zh: 及卒，人士為之傷心，痛悼雖甚，竟不再哭，賓客弔慰，抆淚而已。
units.en: When Shu died, scholars and officials mourned with him. His grief ran deep, yet he would not weep again; when guests came to condole, he merely dabbed at his eyes.
units.literal: When Shu died, men of standing grieved with him; though his mourning ran very deep, he never cried again—when guests came to console him, he only wiped away tears.

units.zh: 其高情達識，開遣滯累，東門吳以還，所未有也。
units.en: In lofty feeling and far-seeing insight, in lifting burdens that weigh on the heart, no one since Dongmen Wu had done the like.
units.literal: His lofty feeling and penetrating insight in dispelling stagnant burdens—since Dongmen Wu, there has been nothing like it.

units.zh: 有集三十卷，見行於世。
units.en: His collected writings ran to thirty scrolls and circulated widely.
units.literal: He had collected works in thirty scrolls, circulating in the world.

units.zh: 子大寶，有文情。
units.en: His son Xing Dabao had a gift for letters.
units.literal: His son Dabao had literary feeling.

units.zh: 孽子大德、大道，略不識字焉。
units.en: His illegitimate sons Dade and Dadao could barely read.
units.literal: Illegitimate sons Dade and Dadao scarcely knew characters at all.

units.zh: 論曰：子才少有盛名，鼓動京洛，文宗學府，獨秀當年，舉必任真，情無飾智，疏通簡易，罕見其人，足為一代之模楷也。
units.en: The appraisal says: Zicai enjoyed a great reputation from youth and stirred the capital and Luoyang. As a master of letters and a repository of learning, he stood alone in his time. His actions were always genuine, his feelings free of clever display; open, accessible, and simple, he was rare indeed and could serve as a model for a generation.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Zicai had a great reputation from youth and stirred the capital and Luoyang. As a master of letters and repository of learning, he alone shone in his time. In action he always followed genuineness, and in feeling he did not embellish his intelligence. Open, accessible, and simple, such a man was rarely seen and was enough to be a model for a generation.

units.zh: 及明崔甗之謗言，執侯景之奸使，昔人稱孟軻為勇，于文簡公見之。
units.en: When he exposed Cui Yan's slander and seized Hou Jing's treacherous envoy, one can see in Duke Wenjian the courage that earlier men praised in Meng Ke.
units.literal: When he exposed Cui Yan's slanderous words and seized Hou Jing's treacherous envoy, what men of old called Meng Ke's courage can be seen in Duke Wenjian.

units.zh: 唯嘗短崔暹，頗為累德。
units.en: Only his past disparagement of Cui Xian somewhat blemished his virtue.
units.literal: Only, he once disparaged Cui Xian, and this rather blemished his virtue.

units.zh: 阮籍未嘗品藻人物，斯亦良有以焉。
units.en: Ruan Ji never passed judgment on people, and there was good reason for that.
units.literal: Ruan Ji never appraised people; this too had good reason.

units.zh: 孔、墨、荀、孟稟聖賢之資，弘正道以勵其俗。
units.en: Confucius, Mozi, Xunzi, and Mencius were endowed with the gifts of sages and worthies and championed the true Way to stir their contemporaries toward better conduct.
units.literal: Confucius, Mozi, Xunzi, and Mencius received the endowment of sages and worthies and enlarged the correct Way to encourage their peoples.

units.zh: 初，文宣命邢卲制帝名殷，字正道，帝從而尤之曰：「殷家弟及，『正』字一止，吾身後兒不得也。」
units.en: Earlier, Emperor Wenxuan had ordered Xing Shao to devise Yin as the emperor's personal name and Zhengdao as his style. Wenxuan later faulted him for it: "In the house of Yin, brothers succeeded one another, and the character 正 contains a single 'stop.' After I am gone, my son will not have it."
units.literal: Initially, Emperor Wenxuan ordered Xing Shao to devise the emperor's personal name Yin and style Zhengdao; the emperor then faulted him, saying, "In the house of Yin, younger brothers succeeded; the character zheng contains one stop, so after I am gone my son will not get it."

units.zh: 卲懼，請改焉。
units.en: Shao was frightened and asked to change the names.
units.literal: Shao was afraid and asked to change it.

units.zh: 以太子少傅魏收為兼尚書右僕射。
units.en: Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Wei Shou was made Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince Wei Shou was appointed Concurrent Right Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 己卯，兼右僕射魏收以阿縱除名。
units.en: On the jimao day, Concurrent Right Vice Director Wei Shou was dismissed from office for fawning and indulgence.
units.literal: On the jimao day, Concurrent Right Deputy Director Wei Shou was dismissed from office for fawning and indulgence.

units.zh: 遂奔葛榮，又亡歸尒朱榮於秀容。
units.en: He fled next to Ge Rong, then broke away again and took refuge with Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.
units.literal: He then fled to Ge Rong, and again broke away and returned to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.

units.zh: 先是，劉貴事榮，盛言神武美，至是始得見，以憔悴故，未之奇也。
units.en: Liu Gui had long served Erzhu Rong and spoken lavishly of Gao Huan's gifts; now Gao Huan finally met Rong face to face, but worn and haggard as he was, Rong saw nothing remarkable in him.
units.literal: Earlier Liu Gui had served Rong and lavishly praised Shenwu's excellence; only now did he first gain an audience, but because he was haggard, Rong did not regard him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 旣而榮以神武為親信都督。
units.en: Soon after, Erzhu Rong appointed Gao Huan trusted commander.
units.literal: Shortly thereafter Rong made Shenwu trusted commander.

units.zh: 于於時魏明帝銜鄭儼、徐紇，逼靈太后，未敢制，私使榮舉兵內向。
units.en: At that time Emperor Ming of Northern Wei loathed Zheng Yan and Xu He, who dominated Empress Dowager Ling, but dared not move against them openly; he secretly urged Erzhu Rong to march on the capital.
units.literal: At this time Wei Emperor Ming bore hatred for Zheng Yan and Xu He, who pressed the Empress Dowager Ling; he dared not restrain them and secretly sent Rong to raise troops inward.

units.zh: 及尒朱榮擊葛榮，令神武喻下賊別稱王者七人。
units.en: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, he sent Gao Huan to talk seven rebel kings into surrender.
units.literal: When Erzhu Rong attacked Ge Rong, he had Shenwu persuade seven bandit chiefs styling themselves kings to submit.

units.zh: 累遷第三鎮人酋長，常在榮帳內。
units.en: He rose to become chief of the third garrison peoples and remained constantly at Erzhu Rong's side.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief of the third garrison populations and was constantly within Rong's tent.

units.zh: 於是大聚斂，因劉貴貨榮下要人，盡得其意。
units.en: Gao Huan amassed wealth on a grand scale and, through Liu Gui, bought off Erzhu Rong's inner circle until he knew their minds completely.
units.literal: Thereupon he greatly gathered riches; through Liu Gui he bribed Rong's key men and came fully to know their intentions.

units.zh: 時州庫角無故自鳴，神武異之，無幾而孝莊誅榮。
units.en: About then a horn in the provincial storehouse sounded of its own accord; Gao Huan took it for an omen—and soon Emperor Xiaozhuang killed Erzhu Rong.
units.literal: At the time the horn of the provincial storehouse spontaneously sounded without cause; Shenwu took it as strange; before long Xiaozhuang executed Rong.

units.zh: 因隨榮之廄。
units.en: He then followed Rong into the stables.
units.literal: Thereupon he followed Rong to the stables.

units.zh: 廄有惡馬，榮命翦之。
units.en: A vicious stallion was in the stable, and Rong ordered its mane clipped.
units.literal: In the stable there was a vicious horse; Rong ordered its mane clipped.

units.zh: 榮遂坐神武於床下，屏左右而訪時事。
units.en: Rong then seated Gao Huan below his couch, dismissed his attendants, and questioned him on the state of the realm.
units.literal: Rong thereupon seated Shenwu below his couch, dismissed those on either side, and inquired about current affairs.

units.zh: 榮曰：「但言爾意。」
units.en: Rong replied, "Tell me what you have in mind."
units.literal: Rong said: "Just speak your mind."

units.zh: 榮大悅，語自日中至夜半，乃出。
units.en: Rong was delighted; they talked from noon until midnight before Gao Huan left.
units.literal: Rong was greatly pleased; they spoke from midday until midnight before he departed.

units.zh: 後從榮徙據幷州，抵揚州邑人龐蒼鷹，止團焦中。
units.en: Later, when Rong shifted his base to Bing Province, Gao Huan stayed with Pang Cangying of Yangzhou township in a round-walled compound called Tuanjiao.
units.literal: Later following Rong he moved to hold Bing Province, arrived at Pang Cangying of Yangzhou township, and lodged in a round walled compound.

units.zh: 榮以神武為前鋒。
units.en: Rong made Gao Huan his vanguard.
units.literal: Rong made Shenwu vanguard.

units.zh: 及帝暴崩，榮遂入洛，因將篡位。
units.en: When the emperor died suddenly, Rong entered Luoyang and prepared to seize the throne himself.
units.literal: When the emperor suddenly died, Rong then entered Luoyang and intended to usurp the throne.

units.zh: 榮嘗問左右曰：「一日無我，誰可主軍？」
units.en: Rong once asked his companions, "If I were gone, who could lead these armies?"
units.literal: Rong once asked those beside him: "One day without me — who could command the army?"

units.zh: 以明公雄武，乘時奮發，討鄭儼、徐紇而清帝側，霸業可舉鞭而成。
units.en: With your might, my lord, rise now, strike down Zheng Yan and Xu He, cleanse the emperor's side—and dominion over the realm is yours at a flick of the whip.
units.literal: With your heroic martial power, sir, if you seize the moment and strike, punish Zheng Yan and Xu He and cleanse the emperor's side — hegemony can be achieved at a flick of the whip.

units.zh: 皆稱尒朱兆。
units.en: All named Erzhu Zhao.
units.literal: All named Erzhu Zhao.

units.zh: 因誡兆曰：「爾非其匹，終當為其穿鼻。」
units.en: He warned Zhao, "You are no match for him; in the end he will put the ring in your nose."
units.literal: He thereupon warned Zhao: "You are not his match; in the end you will be bridled by him."

units.zh: 至上黨，明帝又私詔停之。
units.en: When the army reached Shangdang, the emperor secretly ordered a halt.
units.literal: Reaching Shangdang, Ming again privately ordered him to halt.

units.zh: 曰：「此正可統三千騎以還，堪代我主衆者，唯賀六渾耳。」
units.en: Rong said, "Zhao can lead three thousand horsemen home, but only Heiliuhun is fit to replace me in command of the host."
units.literal: He said: "This one can just lead three thousand cavalry back; the man fit to replace me in commanding the masses is only Heiliuhun."

units.zh: 神武諫，恐不聽，請鑄像卜之，鑄不成，乃止。
units.en: Gao Huan remonstrated; fearing Rong would not heed him, he had a Buddha image cast for divination—and when the casting failed, Rong abandoned the plan.
units.literal: Shenwu remonstrated; fearing he would not listen, he asked to cast an image and divined by it; the casting did not succeed, and so Rong stopped.

units.zh: 劉向云戰國時劉氏自秦獲於魏。
units.en: Liu Xiang said that in the Warring States period the Liu clan was captured from Qin by Wei.
units.literal: Liu Xiang said that in the Warring States period the Liu clan was captured from Qin by Wei.

units.zh: 文襄乃奏吏部郎崔暹為御史中尉，糾劾權豪，無所縱捨，於是風俗更始，私枉路絕。
units.en: Gao Cheng then had Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful without sparing any, custom was renewed, and private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.
units.literal: Wenxiang then memorialized to make Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful and wealthy without sparing any, and custom was renewed — private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.

units.zh: 領軍元叉，太后之妹夫也，恃寵驕盈。
units.en: Yuan Cha, the dowager's brother-in-law and commander of the guards, grew insolent on favor.
units.literal: Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha, the empress dowager's sister's husband, relied on favor and was arrogant to excess.

units.zh: 及清河王懌為元叉所害，悅了無讎恨之意，乃以桑落酒候伺之，盡其私佞。
units.en: When Qinghe Wang Yi fell to Yuan Cha, Yue bore no grudge; he courted Cha with mulberry-fall wine and shameless flattery.
units.literal: When Qinghe Wang Yi was killed by Yuan Cha, Yue had not the slightest thought of vengeance; he waited on him with mulberry-fall wine and exhausted private flattery.

units.zh: 懌裁之以法，每抑黜之，為叉所疾。
units.en: Yi checked him with law and repeatedly humiliated him; Cha came to hate him.
units.literal: Yi restrained him by law and each time demoted and disgraced him; Cha therefore hated him.

units.zh: 叉黨人通直郎宋維希叉旨，[7]告懌謀反，禁懌門下，訊問左右及朝貴，貴人分明，乃得雪釋焉。
units.en: Cha's man Song Wei, eager to please, [7] accused Yi of treason; they sealed his staff and questioned attendants and nobles until the truth cleared him.
units.literal: A partisan of Cha, Direct-Gate Gentleman Song Wei, pleased to Cha's intent, [7] reported that Yi plotted rebellion; they sealed Yi's Gate and Chamber staff, questioned his attendants and court nobles—the noble accounts were clear, and he was only then cleared and released.

units.zh: 正光元年七月，叉與劉騰逼肅宗於顯陽殿，閉靈太后於後宮，囚懌於門下省，誣懌罪狀，遂害之，時年三十四。
units.en: In the first year of Zhenguang, seventh month, Cha and Liu Teng seized Xiaoming in Xianyang Hall, walled the dowager in the rear palace, jailed Yi in the Gate and Chamber office, forged charges, and killed him at thirty-four.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhenguang, Cha with Liu Teng forced Emperor Suzong in Xianyang Hall, shut Empress Dowager Ling in the rear palace, imprisoned Yi in the Gate and Chamber office, fabricated Yi's crimes, and killed him; he was thirty-four.

units.zh: 叉大喜，以悅為侍中、太尉。
units.en: Cha was delighted and made him palace attendant and grand marshal.
units.literal: Cha was greatly pleased and made Yue Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 魏孝明嘉之，賜縑百疋。
units.en: Emperor Xiaoming of Wei praised him and bestowed a hundred bolts of silk.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaoming of Wei praised him and bestowed a hundred bolts of silk.

units.zh: 魏帝召而謂之曰：「卿風度峻整，姿貌秀異，後當升進，何以處官？」
units.en: The Wei emperor summoned him and said, "Your bearing is stern and composed, your appearance outstanding; you will rise in rank — what office do you desire?"
units.literal: The Wei emperor summoned him and said, "Your bearing is stern and composed, your appearance outstanding; you will rise in rank — what office do you desire?"

units.zh: 正光中，行洛陽令，部內肅然。
units.en: In the Zhenguang era he acted as magistrate of Luoyang; within his district all was orderly.
units.literal: In the Zhenguang era he acted as magistrate of Luoyang; within his district all was orderly.

units.zh: 令楊愔傳旨，謂國子助教許散愁曰：「先生在世何以自資？」
units.en: He had Yang Yin deliver his message to Xu Sanchou, assistant instructor at the National University: "Sir, how do you occupy yourself in this life?"
units.literal: He had Yang Yin convey the imperial message and say to National University assistant instructor Xu Sanchou, "Sir, in this life by what do you support yourself?"

units.zh: 乙巳，太師、常山王演矯詔誅尚書令楊愔、尚書右僕射燕子獻、領軍大將軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道、散騎常侍鄭子默。
units.en: On the yisi day Prince Yan of Changshan, grand preceptor, forged an edict and had executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director; Kezhuhun Tianhe, commanding general of the palace guards; Song Qindao, palace attendant; and Zheng Zimo, attendant of the scattered cavalry.
units.literal: On the yisi day the grand preceptor, Prince of Changshan Yan, forged an edict and executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Kezhuhun Tianhe, general-in-chief commanding the guards; Song Qindao, attendant at the palace; and Zheng Zimo, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

units.zh: 及承大位，楊愔、燕子獻、宋欽道等同輔。
units.en: When he came to the throne, Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Song Qindao, and others served jointly as his advisers.
units.literal: When he inherited the great throne, Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Song Qindao, and others assisted him together.

units.zh: 以常山王地親望重，內外畏服，加以文宣初崩之日，太后本欲立之，故愔等並懷猜忌。
units.en: Prince Yan of Changshan was a close kinsman with formidable prestige, feared and obeyed at court and beyond. Since the empress dowager had originally wanted to enthrone him when Emperor Wenxuan died, Yang Yin and the others all suspected him.
units.literal: Because the Prince of Changshan was close in kinship and weighty in reputation, and those within and without feared and submitted to him, and because on the day Emperor Wenxuan first died the empress dowager had originally wanted to enthrone him, Yin and the others all harbored suspicion.

units.zh: 股肱輔弼，雖懷厥誠，旣不能贊弘道德，和睦親懿，又不能遠慮防身，深謀衛主，應斷不斷，自取其咎。
units.en: His chief ministers may have been sincere, but they could not help him enlarge the Way and virtue or keep harmony among his kin. Nor could they plan far enough to protect themselves or safeguard their lord. When decision was needed they failed to decide, and brought disaster on themselves.
units.literal: His chief ministers and assistants, although they held sincere intentions, could neither assist him in magnifying the Way and virtue and harmonizing his close kin, nor plan farsightedly to protect themselves and deeply scheme to safeguard their lord; when they should have acted decisively they did not, and brought blame upon themselves.

units.zh: 臣旣誅夷，君壽廢辱，皆任非其器之所致爾。
units.en: The ministers were exterminated, and the ruler, though still alive, was deposed and humiliated. All of it came from entrusting affairs to men unequal to the task.
units.literal: The ministers were already executed and wiped out, while the ruler, though alive, was deposed and humiliated; all this came from entrusting office to men who were not equal to the task.

units.zh: 未及科，會幷州定國寺新成，神武謂陳元康、溫子升曰：「昔作《芒山寺碑》文，時稱妙絕，今《定國寺碑》當使誰作詞也？」
units.en: Before the levy was collected, the new Dingguo Temple in Bingzhou was finished. Gao Huan said to Chen Yuankang and Wen Zisheng, "The Mangshan Temple stele was called peerless—who should write the Dingguo Temple stele now?"
units.literal: Before the levy was exacted, the new Dingguo Temple in Bingzhou was completed; Gao Huan said to Chen Yuankang and Wen Zisheng, "When we composed the Mangshan Temple stele text it was called peerless—now for the Dingguo Temple stele whose words should compose it?"

units.zh: 壬寅，魏帝詔太原公洋攝理軍國，遣中使敦喻。
units.en: On renyin day the emperor issued an edict that Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang administer military and state affairs and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.
units.literal: On renyin the Wei Emperor issued an edict that Duke of Taiyuan Yang administer military and state affairs, and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.

units.zh: 時太原公洋在城東雙堂，入而討賊，臠割京等，皆漆其頭。
units.en: At the time Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.
units.literal: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.

units.zh: 與懷朔省事雲中司馬子如及秀容人劉貴、中山人賈顯智為奔走之友，懷朔戶曹史孫騰、外兵史侯景亦相友結。
units.en: He made running companions of Sima Ziru, affairs clerk at Huaishuo's Yunzhong desk, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan; Sun Teng, the garrison household clerk, and Hou Jing, clerk for external military affairs, joined their circle as well.
units.literal: With Sima Ziru, affairs clerk of Yunzhong at Huaishuo, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan he formed a band of comrades ready to run errands; Sun Teng, household clerk at Huaishuo, and Hou Jing, clerk in external military affairs, also joined in friendship.

units.zh: 其先遼東襄平人，元魏平定遼東，徙家於代，隨孝文遷洛，遂為洛陽人。
units.en: His forebears came from Xiangping in Liaodong. When the Northern Wei pacified the northeast the family was moved to Dai; they followed Emperor Xiaowen to Luoyang and became Luoyang natives.
units.literal: His ancestors were people of Xiangping in Liaodong; when Northern Wei pacified Liaodong the family moved to Dai, followed Emperor Xiaowen in the move to Luoyang, and thus became Luoyang people.

units.zh: 周文翼翼，翔此靈禽。
units.en: King Wen of Zhou, reverent and careful, here saw this numinous bird soar.
units.literal: Zhou Wen diligent and reverent, this numinous bird soared here.

units.zh: 後吏部尚書李神儁奏言，比因多故，常侍遂無員限，今以王元景等為常侍，定限八員。
units.en: Later Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun memorialized that because of many disturbances the attendant-at-court posts had long had no fixed quota; now Wang Yuanjing and others were made attendants, fixed at eight.
units.literal: Later Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun memorialized saying that because of many disturbances the attendant-at-court posts had long had no fixed quota; now Wang Yuanjing and others were made attendants, fixed at eight.

units.zh: 魏靜帝於顯陽殿講《孝經》、《禮記》，繪與從弟騫、裴伯茂、魏收、盧元明等俱為錄議。
units.en: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites at the Xianyang Hall; Hui and his cousin Qian, Pei Bomo, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others were all recorders and discussants.
units.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites at the Xianyang Hall; Hui and his cousin Qian, Pei Bomo, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others were all recorders and discussants.

units.zh: 李渾 子湛 渾弟繪 族子公緒 李璵 弟瑾 族弟曉 鄭述祖 子元德
units.en: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande
units.literal: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande

units.zh: 世宗給其工力 諸本「世宗」作「世祖」，北史卷八八作「宣武」。
units.en: "The emperor gave him laborers": editions read "ancestral emperor"; Northern History scroll 88 reads "Xuanwu."
units.literal: The emperor gave him laborers: in various editions "emperor" reads "ancestral emperor"; Northern History scroll 88 reads "Xuanwu."

units.zh: 按上已見「世宗」，「祖」是「宗」之訛，今據改。
units.en: "Emperor" already appears above; "ancestral" is a corruption of "emperor"—corrected here.
units.literal: Since "emperor" already appears above, "ancestral" is an error for "emperor"—now corrected accordingly.

units.zh: 其年，四門小學博士孔璠等學官四十五人上書曰：「竊見故處士趙郡李謐：十歲喪父，哀號罷隣人之相；
units.en: That year Kong Fan, Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School, and forty-five academic officers memorialized: "We observe the former recluse Li Mi of Zhao: at ten he lost his father and wailed until neighbors ceased condoling one another;
units.literal: That year, Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School Kong Fan and forty-five academic officers memorialized, saying: "We have observed the former recluse of Zhao commandery, Li Mi: at ten he lost his father, wailing until neighbors ceased mutual condolence;

units.zh: 昕少與邢卲俱為元羅賓友，及守東萊，卲舉室就之。
units.en: In youth Xin and Xing Shao had both been guests of Yuan Luo; when Xin held Donglai, Shao brought his whole household to join him.
units.literal: In youth Xin and Xing Shao had both been guests of Yuan Luo; when Xin held Donglai, Shao brought his whole household to join him.

units.zh: 譬若以周、邵為丞相，孔丘為御史大夫，太公為將軍，畢公高拾遺於後，弁嚴子為衛尉，皋陶為大理，後稷為司農，伊尹為少府，子贛使外國，顏、閔為博士，子夏為太常，益為右扶風，季路為執金吾，契為鴻臚，龍逢為宗正，伯夷為京兆，管仲為馮翊，魯般為將作，仲山甫為光祿，申伯為太僕，延陵季子為水衡，百里奚為典屬國，柳下惠為大長秋，史魚為司直，蘧伯玉為太傅，孔父為詹事，孫叔敖為諸侯相，子產為郡守，王慶忌為期門，夏育為鼎官，羿為旄頭，宋萬為式道候。」
units.en: Imagine the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao as your chancellors; Confucius as chief censor; the Grand Duke as commander; Duke Bi Gao as court remonstrant; Bian Zhuangzi as captain of the guard; Gao Yao as chief judge; Hou Ji as minister of agriculture; Yi Yin as palace treasurer; Zigong as foreign envoy; Yan Hui and Min Ziqian as court scholars; Zixia as master of rites; Yi as western capital intendant; Zilu as capital commandant; Xie as master of guest ceremonies; Guan Longpeng as keeper of the imperial genealogy; the minister Boyi as metropolitan governor; Guan Zhong as northern capital intendant; Lu Ban as chief engineer; Zhong Shanfu as palace chamberlain; the Earl of Shen as master of the horse; Prince Jizi of Yanling as keeper of parks and waters; Baili Xi as commissioner for dependent peoples; Liuxia Hui as chamberlain to the empress; Shi Yu as censor of conduct; Qu Boyu as grand tutor; Kong Fu as supervisor of the heir apparent's household; Sunshu Ao as chancellor to the feudal lords; Zichan as commandery governor; Prince Qingji as a palace gate guard; Xia Yu as cauldron officer; Yi the Archer as vanguard officer; and Song Wan as road-clearing scout."
units.literal: It is as if you had made the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao your chancellors; Confucius your Censor-in-Chief; the Grand Duke your general; Duke Bi Gao your remonstrant at the rear; Bian Zhuangzi your Commandant of the Guards; Gao Yao your Chief Justice; Hou Ji your Minister of Agriculture; Yi Yin your Privy Treasurer; Zigong your envoy abroad; Yan Hui and Min Ziqian your Erudites; Zixia your Minister of Ceremonies; Yi your western capital intendant; Zilu your Capital Commandant; Xie your Grand Herald; Guan Longpeng your Director of the Imperial Clan; the minister Boyi your Metropolitan Governor; Guan Zhong your northern capital intendant; Lu Ban your Superintendent of Works; Zhong Shanfu your Chamberlain for Attendants; the Earl of Shen your Grand Coachman; Prince Jizi of Yanling your Superintendent of Waters and Parks; Baili Xi your Director of Dependent States; Liuxia Hui your Chamberlain for the Empress; Shi Yu your Rectifier; Qu Boyu your Grand Tutor; Kong Fu your supervisor of the heir apparent's household; Sunshu Ao your chancellor to the feudal lords; Zichan your commandery governor; Prince Qingji your Palace Gate Guard; Xia Yu your Cauldron Officer; Yi the Archer your Vanguard Officer; and Song Wan your road-clearing scout."

units.zh: 魏自崔亮以後。
units.en: In Northern Wei, since the time of Cui Liang,
units.literal: In Wei, since Cui Liang's time.
